chunks.text:
Trazodone is an antidepressant that belongs to a group of drugs called serotonin receptor antagonists and reuptake inhibitors (SARIs).
Trazodone is not a true member of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) class of antidepressants.
Trazodone shares many properties of the SSRIs.
Trazodone is used to treat major depressive disorder.
Trazodone may help to improve your mood.
Trazodone may help to improve your appetite.
Trazodone may help to improve your energy level.
Trazodone may help to decrease anxiety related to depression.
Trazodone may help to decrease insomnia related to depression.
Trazodone works by helping to restore the balance of a certain natural chemical (serotonin) in the brain.

Your family or other caregivers should also be alert to changes in your mood or symptoms.
Report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor.

chunks.text:
Take trazodone exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take trazodone after a meal or a snack.
Trazodone may take up to 2 weeks before your symptoms improve.
Keep using the medication as directed.
Tell your doctor if your symptoms do not improve.
You should not stop using trazodone suddenly.
You could have unpleasant symptoms.
These symptoms include dizziness, vomiting, agitation, sweating, confusion, numbness, tingling, or electric shock feelings.
Ask your doctor how to safely stop using trazodone.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.
If you are using the oral solution, throw away any unused medicine 20 days after first opening the bottle.

chunks.text:
Usual Adult Dose for Depression:
The initial dose is 150 mg orally per day in divided doses.
The dose may be increased by 50 mg orally per day every 3 to 4 days.
The maximum dose for inpatients is 600 mg/day.
The maximum dose for outpatients is 400 mg/day.
Patients should be screened for a personal or family history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania prior to initiating treatment.
-Patients should be monitored for withdrawal symptoms when discontinuing therapy.
Dosage may be gradually reduced.
The reduction depends on therapeutic response.
This occurs after an adequate response has been reached.
If drowsiness develops, a major portion of the daily dose may be administered at bedtime.
If drowsiness develops, a reduction of dosage may be necessary.
-Trazodone should be taken shortly after a meal or light snack.
Use: Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD)

Take the medicine as soon as you can.
Skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose.
Do not take two doses at one time.
